📚 Southern Sociological Theory (Global Knowledge Movements in Social Science) | Author: Raewyn Connell | Translator: Hadi Nouri | First Edition | Naqd-e Farhang Publishing | 1405 | The book Southern Sociological Theory offers a framework for radically rethinking the social sciences and their relationship to knowledge, power, and democracy on a global scale—not merely within Western cultural frameworks. The mainstream of social science presents an image of the world as drawn by educated and affluent people in Europe and North America. Theorists from the countries of the Global North dominate the minds, feelings, and imaginations of social scientists and the list of study topics for students around the world. For most of modern history, the majority of the world has been regarded by social science as merely a source of data. Yet the Global South is engaged in producing knowledge and understanding of society. Through vivid narratives about critics and theorists, Raewyn Connell shows how social theory about the world—from Sayyid Jamal al-Din Asadabadi at the dawn of modern social science to Raúl Prebisch in the process of Latin American industrialization, Ali Shariati in revolutionary Iran, Paulin Hountondji in postcolonial Benin, Veena Das and Ashis Nandy in contemporary India, and many others—holds power and significance for understanding our changing world. With clarity and verve, Southern Sociological Theory introduces readers to texts, ideas, and debates that have emerged from the heart of Indigenous peoples in Australia, Africa, Latin America, and South and Southwest Asia. Dr. Farshad…

◇ When labeling takes the place of science and expert opinion

Dr. Farshad Momeni, criticizing the public sphere's descent into "left versus right" dichotomies and Heydari-Nemati-style squabbles, stresses that many of these labels bear no relation to science or national interests. Instead, he argues, attention must be paid to the "capture of the power structure" by usurers, brokers, and large-scale importers.

Citing studies on the effects of importing manufactured goods that could be produced domestically, he highlights the relationship between imports, employment, and national production, and also references Mohammad Naghizadeh's research on the job-destroying consequences of imports and the sale of raw materials.

In closing, Momeni calls on the government and the media to stop turning a blind eye to the main centers of threat to the national system, and instead — by raising the level of expertise and refraining from labeling — to pave the way for a scientific dialogue on national interests, national independence, and social justice.

🎥 Dr. Farshad Momeni
